expectations.text: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
response.md is written in Ukrainian
Response states the analysed period (months or dates)
Every growth/decline claim carries an uncertainty measure (interval or explicit confidence level)
expectations.evidence: Every language has an interval and confidence

expectations.text: Response names the Wikipedia articles (or article basket/proxies) that were measured
expectations.evidence: Measured via the 'English language' articles (Q1860); titles not listed in the reply, only in the summary

expectations.text: Response ranks or prioritises the five language audiences explicitly
expectations.evidence: Top 3: VI, ES, DE; avoid PL, TR

expectations.text: Ranking reasons use both audience size and growth (or intensity), not just one number
expectations.evidence: Uses size, growth, intensity and ranking score

expectations.text: Response mentions that a language edition is not the same as a country (or gives a reader-geography caveat)
expectations.evidence: Notes that VN/TR are withheld from country data and that the real audience is there

expectations.text: Response notes that Wikipedia interest is not purchase intent or recommends validating with another signal
expectations.evidence: 'це сигнал цікавості, а не гарантія купівельної готовності'

expectations.text: Does not describe a change whose 95% interval crosses zero as growth (e.g. Turkish +7% [-20%, +43%] is 'no clear change')
Reasons are grounded in the data: no unsupported outside claims (competition, market size, demographics) or misreadings of the metrics presented as findings
expectations.evidence: Unsupported: 'Менша конкуренція від локальних сервісів', 'Зростаючий стартап-сектор у В'єтнамі', 'Контент-гап ... для іспаномовців'. The general 'English language' article is used as a learning proxy without noting that it is weaker than exam articles
